ov: Long-haired domesticated cattle of the Himalayas, the Tibetan Plateau and the mountains of Central Asia, north to Mongolia and Siberia. It is descended from the wild yak.

why.dm: Most yaks are domestic; they descend from the wild yak, a separate species.

rg: The Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, Pamirs and Tajikistan, north to Mongolia and Siberia.

cf.tip: Yaks are close relatives of cattle and bison, adapted to high altitude.

notes: The existing fact is half confirmed: yaks have larger lungs and hearts than lowland cattle and carry more oxygen in their blood, keeping foetal haemoglobin all their lives. The 5,000 m figure isn’t in the article. Suggested wording: "Its blood carries more oxygen than a cow’s, because it keeps foetal haemoglobin all its life."
